messages.subject: Small update to poppr (version 1.1.3) and News
messages.subject_clean: Small update to poppr (version 1.1.3) and News
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

Poppr has been updated

This is a small announcement that poppr has been updated and is on CRAN now. Updates for mac and windows should be up within the next couple of days. Version 1.1.3 mainly contains minor improvements and bug fixes. Details can be found here:

version 1.1.3 release notes
 <https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/releases/tag/v.1.1.3>

 <https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/releases/tag/v.1.1.3>
One thing I would like to point out is the improved flexibility of the function plot_poppr_msn. It now allows you to adjust the size of the nodes and choose what MLGs are labeled.

Feature requests

Thibaut Jombart, author of the R package adegenet <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/adegenet/index.html> has recently announced a call for feature requests in this email to the adegenet mailing list <http://lists.r-forge.r-project.org/pipermail/adegenet-forum/2015-February/001067.html> due to the upcoming Population Genetics Hackathon at NESCent <http://www.nescent.org/cal/calendar_detail_pg.php?id=1130>. If you have any feature requests for the adegenet package, follow the link in the email. If you have any feature requests for poppr specifically, you can make them on github: https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/issues (you will need a github account).

Cheers,
Zhian

messages.subject: export tree
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am new to poppr. I was able to load, convert and run my analysis correctly. However, I was wondering if there is any option to export a tree in a generic forma (e.g. newick) to load in specific tree rendering programs.

Any help is appreciated.
Best,
Thiago

messages.subject: Re: export tree
messages.body_plain:
Hi Thiago,

You can export a tree using the function "write.nexus" <http://www.r-phylo.org/wiki/HowTo/InputtingTrees> from the package "ape".

Special tip: If you want to add tip colors to your tree for use in FigTree <http://tree.bio.ed.ac.uk/software/figtree/>, you can use the function add.tip.colors from this gist <https://gist.github.com/zkamvar/3c3f12926de648431937>.

Cheers,
Zhian

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Re: export tree
messages.body_plain:
Hi Thiago,

You can compare populations by converting your data to a genpop object:

obj.pop <- genind2genpop(obj)

proj <- aboot(obj.pop, sample = 1000, dist = rogers.dist) # This should go really fast.

Cheers,
Zhian
